name: Backchannel
tagline: HN, Bluesky, and Reddit discussions merged into one thread
description: Backchannel is a userscript that blends Hacker News, Bluesky, and Reddit discussions into a single merged conversation on any article page. Every page you land on gets checked against the sources you have enabled, so you find out a discussion exists without going hunting for one. Quotes in the comments are matched back to the article and lit as annotations, and clicking a highlight filters the thread to the people discussing that passage. You can vote, reply, and even submit on supported sources using the session you already have, in a popup on news.ycombinator.com. It also blends all of your sources into a custom front page, and includes quality-of-life touches like indent guides, OP marking, and new-comment highlighting. There is no backend, no analytics, and no telemetry — one file with no build step, and a per-site off switch. Formerly known as HNewhere.
highlights: Merges HN, Bluesky, and Reddit threads into one sidebar conversation per article
Quotes in comments are annotated back onto the article text
Vote, reply, and submit with your existing session — the script never sees passwords
No backend, no analytics, no telemetry; one file with no build step
Custom blended front page across all of your enabled sources
curatorNote: A clever browser-userscript mashup that puts HN, Bluesky, and Reddit in one view, featured on the trending list within a week of launch. The annotation layer — quotes matched back to the article — is the feature that makes it feel like a commentary track rather than a comment box.
